title: Training Note for Family Services Center Staff: Instrument Returns, Late Fees and Presumed Loss in the Fine Arts Instrument Usage Program
content:
**The rule.** Under the Fine Arts Instrument Usage Program an instrument is due back on its due-back date, and within the withdrawal return period of calendar days after the last day of attendance when the student withdraws. An instrument turned in after its due-back date is charged the late fee per day for each calendar day late, never more than the maximum late fee per checkout. An instrument returned uncleaned or with personal items in the case is charged the uncleaned return fee. An instrument still not turned in the presumed-lost period of calendar days after the due-back date is treated as lost and charged the replacement charge as an unreturned instrument, per instrument for a pair.

The figures named here (due-back dates, the late fee per day, the maximum late fee, the uncleaned return fee, the withdrawal and presumed-lost periods, the replacement charge) are those of the instrument's usage type.

## Questions answered

**When does a checkout become overdue?** An instrument not turned in by its due-back date becomes overdue on the day after the due-back date.

**How are the days late counted?** The days late are the calendar days between the checkout's due-back date and the date the instrument is turned in. A return on the day after the due-back date is one day late.

**How is the late fee worked out?** The late fee per day is multiplied by the days late, and the result is limited to the maximum late fee per checkout: the fee charged is the lesser of the two. The late fee is posted on the date the overdue instrument is turned in.

**What if the student withdraws from the district?** The instrument must be returned within the withdrawal return period of calendar days after the student's last day of attendance.

**What is an uncleaned return?** An instrument returned without the required cleaning, or with personal items left in the case. Either one is charged the uncleaned return fee.

**When is an unreturned instrument treated as lost?** When it is still not turned in the presumed-lost period of calendar days after the due-back date, the due-back date being day 0. It is then charged the replacement charge as an unreturned instrument; for a home-and-school pair the charge is per instrument.

## Worked figures on hypothetical inputs

The rates below are hypothetical, chosen to show the arithmetic: a late fee of 3.00 per day and a maximum of 45.00.

| Due-back date | Turned in | Days late | Late fee per day multiplied by days late | Late fee charged |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| a Friday | the following Tuesday | 4 | 12.00 | 12.00 |
| a given day | 15 days later | 15 | 45.00 | 45.00 |
| a given day | 20 days later | 20 | 60.00 | 45.00 |

**Presumed loss, hypothetical period of 30 days.** An instrument turned in 12 days after its due-back date is a late return and is charged a late fee. An instrument still not turned in 40 days after its due-back date has passed the period and is treated as lost; a home-and-school pair in that position is charged the replacement charge twice, once for each instrument.

**Uncleaned return.** An instrument turned in on its due-back date with personal items in the case is charged the uncleaned return fee and no late fee.
